Christ Emmanuel

Icons

Christ

Christ Emmanuel

Christ Immanuel · Savior Emmanuel

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Isaiah 7:14

Matthew 1:22–23

King James Version · Scripture previews

Christ Emmanuel represents Christ as a child or young person. Basilica’s explanation links the title with Isaiah’s prophecy and Matthew’s interpretation of Emmanuel as God with us, rather than limiting the image to a particular episode of infancy.

[1] Heading Christ Emmanuel

What is depicted

The displayed Russian icon presents the youthful face of Christ within a halo. The object is catalogued at the National Museum of Tatarstan as an eighteenth-century work in tempera on a prepared wooden panel; the photograph carries its own Creative Commons licence.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

History and tradition

This catalogue date identifies the particular Russian panel. It should be distinguished from the much earlier scriptural name Emmanuel and from other representations of the child Christ, including Nativity scenes and images with his mother.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

Published explanation

Basilica interprets the combination of youthful appearance, mature facial features and a high forehead as expressing both Christ’s human life and divine wisdom. The article explicitly relates the composition to Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23.

[1] Christ Emmanuel: appearance and prophetic title

Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.

[3] Matthew 1:22–23
